result.summary: Implemented the approved design verbatim. (1) test/support/tenant_slug.ex: added `@spec unique_realm(prefix :: String.t()) :: String.t()` / `def unique_realm(prefix \\ "realm") when is_binary(prefix), do: "#{prefix}-" <> Ecto.UUID.generate()`, plus one moduledoc sentence noting it also fixes ISS-0878 (mirrors the existing ISS-0059 callout). (2) auth_pipeline_test.exs:64-66 and identity_test.exs:80-82 private defp bodies now call `Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_realm(prefix)` (identity_test.exs keeps its `\\ "realm"` default, per design). (3) authorization_ac9_test.exs:49 single-line defp now delegates the same way. (4) provider_registry_multi_realm_test.exs:83 delegates via the bare `TenantSlugFixture.unique_realm(prefix)` form since the file already has `alias Letflow.TenantSlugFixture` (line 72, confirmed by direct read, not assumed) used elsewhere for `unique_slug/1`-style calls; also corrected its moduledoc line ~30 from 'unique_realm/1 (System.unique_integer/1-suffixed)' to 'unique_realm/1 (UUID-suffixed)'. No call sites, assertions, or test descriptions changed anywhere. No lib/ or priv/repo/migrations/ files touched -- confirmed via `git diff origin/main --stat`, only test/support/tenant_slug.ex and the 4 test files appear as changes from this commit (plus pre-existing commits already on the branch: doc-bookkeeping, design artefact, status yaml). Did NOT touch the 3 explicitly-out-of-scope files (auth_pipeline_configurable_verifier_test.exs, mobile_tenant_config_test.exs, tenant_config_test.exs) per the design's scope decision. `mix compile` ran clean, exit 0, no warnings/errors. `mix test test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs test/letflow/api/authorization_ac9_test.exs test/letflow/oidc/provider_registry_multi_realm_test.exs test/letflow/identity_test.exs` -> 'Finished in 185.3 seconds (0.00s async, 185.3s sync) / Result: 84 passed', 0 failures. (test/support/tenant_slug.ex is a support module with no ExUnit tests of its own -- correctness proven by the 84 passing call-site tests, per the design's own stated rationale that a cross-OS-process race isn't exercisable by a single-process test.)
